claims.text: Two counts (sex trafficking of minors; conspiracy), conduct at least 2002 to at least 2005, New York and Palm Beach residences; girls as young as 14; 'massages' becoming sexual; hundreds of dollars cash per encounter; some abused often daily; paid to recruit other girls, recruiter and recruit both paid; employees and associates contacted victims and scheduled; Berman quote.

sources.label: US Attorney's Office SDNY, 'Jeffrey Epstein Charged In Manhattan Federal Court With Sex Trafficking Of Minors', 8 July 2019

claims.text: Convicted 29 Dec 2021 on five of six counts after five days' deliberation; accusers Jane, Kate, Carolyn and Annie Farmer (real name), abused as teens in the 1990s and early 2000s at homes in Florida, New York and New Mexico, one as young as 14; 24 prosecution witnesses incl. a housekeeper and pilots; massage table and a black book listing contacts under 'massages'; bank records showed $30.7m from Epstein to Maxwell; defence: vindictive prosecution, memory expert Elizabeth Loftus; she did not testify.

sources.label: VOA / AP, 'Ghislaine Maxwell convicted in Epstein sex abuse case', 29 Dec 2021

claims.text: Epstein Victims' Compensation Program: about $121m paid to about 150 victims; about 225 claims (double the estimate); 92% offered accepted; about 75 rejected; administrator Jordana Feldman; acceptance barred suits against the estate but not cooperation with law enforcement or speaking publicly.

sources.label: NBC News, 'Jeffrey Epstein victims fund paid out $121 million to about 150', Aug 2021

claims.text: March 2005 a mother reported her 14-year-old daughter was having sex with an adult in a Palm Beach mansion; detectives opened an investigation; Chief Michael Reiter asked State Attorney Barry Krischer to step aside over 'highly unusual' handling, then gave evidence to the FBI; Krischer (July 2019) pointed to a 53-page draft federal indictment Acosta could have pursued; Epstein pleaded guilty to state charges and served 13 months in Palm Beach County jail; Reiter: 'the worst failure of the criminal justice system', 'The stories were all the same.'

sources.label: NBC News, 'Ex-Florida police chief: Epstein case "worst failure" of criminal justice', 2019

entries.topic: Schedulers, the agreement's four names, Brunel

claims.text: The 2008 agreement (per Judge Marra's 2019 opinion) promised no charges against 'any potential co-conspirators', naming Sarah Kellen, Adriana Ross, Lesley Groff and Nadia Marcinkova; a 2019 Jane Doe suit (abuse 2002–05 from age 14) alleges Kellen and Groff scheduled visits, asked her to bring other girls and paid her; Groff's lawyer denied any misconduct; Kellen did not comment; Ross and Marcinkova not named in that suit.

Jean-Luc Brunel detained at Charles de Gaulle in 2020 in the French probe opened after Epstein's US charges; charged with rape of minors (December 2021); found dead in his Paris cell 19 Feb 2022; lawyers said he always maintained his innocence.

claims.text: Vicky Ward says the Farmer sisters' allegations (Annie: abused at the New Mexico ranch in 1996 at 16) were removed from her 2003 Vanity Fair piece shortly before press after Epstein visited editor Graydon Carter; Carter says Ward 'didn't have the goods'; both accounts have shifted.

claims.text: Then Virginia Roberts, 16, summer spa job at Mar-a-Lago where her father worked; met Maxwell there in 2000; offered work as a travelling masseuse; settled with Epstein 2009 ($500,000 per documents unsealed 2022); 2016 defamation suit against Maxwell settled 2017; settlement with Prince Andrew 2022 (reported $16m); Andrew denied the allegations; died 25 April 2025 in Western Australia aged 41, by suicide per her publicist.
2016 deposition, unsealed Jan 2024: 'I don't think Donald Trump participated in anything'; she had never seen him take part, but had heard he had been at Epstein's house.
